title: E2E integration of INT8 weight-only GPTQ/AWQ profiles with sensitivity sweep, drift checks, and fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Integrate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) into our E2E CI/regression pipelines and nightly sensitivity sweeps, add drift detection for profile accuracy regressions, and document a fallback/rollback playbook for serving when profiles cause quality regressions. This ticket covers engineering integration, telemetry hooks, synthetic and real workload validation, and automation for isolating problematic profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly CI job runs GPTQ and AWQ weight-only profile validation across a prioritized model set (small/medium/large) and reports pass/fail status to the dashboard.
Sensitivity sweep (per-layer scale, per-channel vs per-tensor config, block-size) completes within budgeted nightly window and produces a ranked matrix of profiles by accuracy/cost/latency.
Drift detector triggers an alert when post-deploy model-level metric delta exceeds configured thresholds (perplexity > 1.5% OR instruction-following regression > 2%).
Automated rollback/fallback playbook documented and exercised in a canary run; a serving fallback to FP16 or alternate safe profile completes within defined SLO (90s for failover path).
Telemetry capture includes token-level latency, per-request profile-id, calibration seed, and prompt category to enable root-cause analysis.
steps: Add GPTQ & AWQ profile runner to quant-profile service (new flag to select algorithm and block-size).
Create a normalized profile manifest schema (profile-id, algorithm, block_size, per_channel, calibration_corpus_hash, artifacts_link).
Extend nightly CI job to schedule sensitivity sweeps with configurable parameter grid (layer groups, block size, scale fudge factors).
Wire telemetry: emit profile-id, model-version, dataset-tag, eval-metrics (ppl, token-accuracy, delta-ll), and runtime stats (ms/token, throughput).
Implement drift detector job comparing baseline->nightly evals and raising alerts into paging/dashboards.
Author fallback handlers in serving runtime to detect high logit divergence and automatically switch to a validated fallback profile or FP16 path.
Create a canary run on dedicated capacity for one customer-facing model to validate both sensitivity sweep results and rollback logic.
testing_plan: Unit tests for profile manifest parsing and backward compatibility with existing registry format.
Integration test: run GPTQ and AWQ profile generation on a 7B model using small calibration corpus; verify correctness of quantized checkpoint and deterministic inference on fixed prompts.
E2E regression: nightly job runs 50 example prompts (mix of instructions, code, Q&A) and compares metrics against golden baseline; failures create a triage ticket with attachments.
Stress/regtest: simulate high-concurrency serving using new profiles to measure latency P95 and throughput degradation relative to FP16 baseline.
Canary exercise: purposefully inject a bad profile (calibration mismatch) to verify drift detection fires and fallback completes within SLO.

Add metrics: profile_application_count, profile_failure_count, profile_rollback_count, profile_avg_ms_per_token.
Tag test/eval runs with dataset-tag and sweep-params to allow trend analysis in Console.
notes: Trade-offs: running broad sensitivity sweeps nightly increases CI cost and GPU hours; we mitigate by prioritizing models (traffic-weighted) and using smaller calibration corpora for initial sweeps. GPTQ and AWQ can diverge on edge-case instruction-following behavior; plan is to prefer profiles that minimize instruction-follow regression even if slightly more expensive. Risk: calibration drift when production prompts differ from calibration corpus; mitigation: keep calibration corpus representative and add per-customer calibration where possible.
